issues.title: PRD FR-9b / SRS FR-38: fix the call-graph RESOLVER ambiguous bare-name bind
issues.build_status: Root-caused and source-verified. Fix NOT started.
issues.body:
PAIRED DELIVERABLE with V2-009. Shipping V2-009 alone yields a LARGER graph feeding the same broken resolver -- more files, the same wrong hot_nodes and danger_zones, and a HIGHER collided in-degree on the same wrong nodes. prd-v2.md states verbatim: 'FR-9a alone is INSUFFICIENT'. SRS.md:296-297 states the same. FR-9b does not supersede FR-9a and FR-9a does not subsume FR-9b.

THE DEFECT, verified on disk by this planning pass 2026-08-01: langgraph_engine/parsers/graph_model.py:265 reads 'return candidates[0]' -- the third of three returns inside _resolve_target(), reached when a bare simple method name matches multiple known method FQNs and none is in the caller's file. An arbitrary first-match bind with no disambiguation and no confidence marker. Lines 253-254 and 263-264 (the len(candidates) == 1 cases) are legitimate. The dotted path at 243-255 correctly returns unresolved when ambiguous, so the defect is specific to bare names.

MEASURED consequences (by two independent agents; cited, not re-derived by this planning pass):
  list.append()  binds to JsonlAppender.append  (src/mcp/base/persistence.py:222)  in-degree 1592
  str.format()   binds to ErrorMessages.format  (langgraph_engine/error_messages.py:568)  in-degree 755-756 (two agents measured 755 and 756; reported as a range, not adjudicated)
  dict.get()/set() bind to _MemoryLayer.get/set (langgraph_engine/cache_system.py:101 and :113)

55.5 percent of cross-file 'resolved' edges are collision artifacts. Of 26,114 total: 18,608 unresolved + 2,853 builtin-collision + 433 cross-file ambiguity = 21,894, leaving 4,220 high-confidence. Arithmetic checked and exact.

WHY IT IS NOT COSMETIC: sdlc_pipeline/call_graph_analyzer.py builds danger_zones (:303) and hot_nodes (:1197) on an n >= 5 caller-count gate, and _classify_risk (:56-67) labels per-method risk on an 8+ gate. Both are caller-count-only. JsonlAppender.append currently ranks as the codebase's top danger zone on the strength of every list.append() in the repo, and that ranking is injected into the Step 0 planning prompt via prompt_gen_expert_caller.py:179-182 and :204-207.

PRECONDITION VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED: resolve_edges() IS invoked at call_graph_builder_legacy.py:96 on every build. Had it not been, get_edges() would return raw edges and this requirement would be unwarranted.

EXPLICITLY NOT PART OF THIS DEFECT: resolve_edges() writes to _resolved_edges, not graph.edges, so reading graph.edges gives 656 instead of 7,004. NO SHIPPING CODE DOES THIS -- all four consumers use get_edges() (:155, :455, :600, :1209). It caught an agent, not the pipeline. Do not conflate the two.

SIZE IS ASSUMED (5). The one-line source fix is trivial; the cost is the two-field confidence reporting at 6 named consumption points, the committed collision check, and the unit test.

NUMBERING: this is FR-9b, not FR-25. FR-25 is already claimed by a proposed CI check in advisory_items.json and reusing it would create an ID collision.
acceptance_criteria: (1) A committed check enumerates every method FQN appearing in danger_zones or hot_nodes for a full-repo analysis run and FAILS if any entry's simple name collides with a Python builtin or stdlib method name AND its fan-in does not survive once collided edges are excluded. The collision list is derived from builtins plus the str/list/dict/set method sets, not hand-maintained. An entry whose fan-in survives exclusion is legitimate and passes -- the check is on the collision, not on the name.

(2) The high-confidence edge count is reported alongside the raw count as two distinct fields at every point fan-in is consumed: _classify_risk's input, danger_zones.callers_count, hot_nodes.callers_count, and all four graph.get_edges() consumers at call_graph_analyzer.py:155, :455, :600 and :1209. A consumer that reads only one of the two numbers fails review.

(3) graph_model.py:265 no longer returns candidates[0] for an ambiguous bare name -- it returns either the unresolved target or a resolution explicitly marked ambiguous -- and a unit test asserts that a bare name matching 2 or more FQNs with no same-file candidate does NOT produce a confident edge.

The AC deliberately does NOT assert that the 55.5 percent collision rate must fall to any specific figure. No post-fix rate has been measured and pre-committing a target would be a fabrication. It asserts the rate is REPORTED and that assertions (1) and (3) hold.

issues.title: PRD NFR-3 / SRS NFR-9: name the CheckpointManager contract and fix 3 durability defects
issues.build_status: The writer ALREADY EXISTS and is already wired. langgraph_engine/checkpoint_manager.py::CheckpointManager, 9 public methods plus _atomic_write, triggered at every step boundary by core/step_decorator.py. It survives PRD FR-4 untouched.
issues.body:
THE PREMISE THIS WAS ORIGINALLY SIZED ON WAS FALSE. NFR-3 was sized at 8 points / WSJF 3.00 on the Phase 0 claim that post-tool-tracker.py was the sole writer of checkpoint state. HLD OAQ 1 verified against live source that this conflated TWO INDEPENDENT SYSTEMS. Re-scored: size 8 -> 3, WSJF 3.00 -> 6.33.

  System A, step-boundary crash recovery: CheckpointManager, hook-independent, lives entirely outside the three deleted hook packages, with a real resume entry point (orchestrator.py::resume_flow -> quality/recovery_handler.py::resume_from_checkpoint). SURVIVES FR-4 UNTOUCHED. The crash-recovery guarantee was never at risk.
  System B, per-tool-call progress: hooks/post_tool_tracker/progress_tracker.py, finer-grained than any SRS step guarantee. This part genuinely dies with FR-4. Its replacement is the existing mcp-post-tool-tracker server, called as a PROJECTION of the checkpoint record, never an independent writer.

Corrected verdict: this is closer to telemetry loss than crash-recovery loss.

NO DEPENDENCY ON ANY OTHER ISSUE. It sits in batch G only because product-sequencing-v2.md section 1 fixes the D1-D7 gate order and NFR-3 belongs to D6. If work is parallelised it can start at any time.

Blocks V2-027, because the progress projection must exist before the writer that currently produces progress is deleted.
acceptance_criteria: A kill-the-process-mid-pipeline test confirms resume picks up at the correct step boundary using the existing checkpoint writer (no new writer is designed or built).

Defect 1: step_decorator.py:169 no longer swallows a checkpoint-save failure with a warning and continues. It raises, or sets an explicit checkpoint_degraded flag the resume path refuses to trust. A best-effort write cannot back a contractual guarantee.
Defect 2: a second test confirms the per-tool-call progress surface is a PROJECTION of the checkpoint record rather than a second writer, so no dual-write path exists.
Defect 3: a replay-idempotency test confirms re-executing a side-effecting step (e.g. GitHub issue creation) twice with the same session-id-plus-step-number key produces no duplicate external effect.
issues.acceptance_criteria_source: prd-v2.md section 5, NFR-3 row (Phase 2.1 revision per ADR-011 / OAQ 1); SRS.md:756 (NFR-9).

issues.title: PRD FR-8a / SRS FR-19: instrument the Stop hook over 20 invocations and decide each capability
issues.build_status: Measured (statically); work NOT started. hooks/stop_notifier/ has ZERO test coverage -- characterisation tests are a blocking prerequisite for any reduction work.
issues.body:
THE FLOOR FIGURE MOVED AND THE PROBLEM CHANGED SHAPE. Initially measured at 8 spawns per turn (16 with retries). That measurement assumed the gated target scripts exist. 7 of the 9 referenced scripts were verified ABSENT, so their .exists() guards fail and they never spawn. The true floor is approximately 2 -- the unconditional git rev-parse calls.

CONSEQUENCE: FR-8a is NOT primarily an overhead problem. Stop does fire every response turn, but the per-turn cost is small. The real defect is CORRECTNESS, and it is tracked separately as PRD FR-21 (V2-034).

CANNOT BE SATISFIED BY A STATIC RE-DERIVATION. The approximately-2 figure is a static filesystem inference and has NEVER been observed at runtime. The AC requires 20 consecutive REAL invocations with runtime instrumentation. A static re-derivation does not satisfy it.

WHAT SHIPS IN v2.0.0: the instrumentation script, the per-capability decision with a written rationale, and reference retirement for every capability decided 'not rebuilt' (V2-034).
WHAT DEFERS TO v2.1: BUILDING any of the 5 capabilities the decision session selects for rebuild -- auto-save-session, archive-old-sessions, plan-session-archiver, preference-auto-tracker, common-failures-prevention. No D1-D7 gate requires any of them. 'Delete the reference' is a valid end state per capability, not a fallback.

NOTE THE AC'S OWN INCENTIVE: it asserts a per-turn spawn count of at most 2 unless a named exception is documented with a rationale. Every capability rebuilt that adds a spawn must individually clear that bar. Rebuilding is a cost this FR was written to constrain, not a free win.
acceptance_criteria: A committed instrumentation script reports, for 20 consecutive REAL Stop-hook invocations on this repo's current checkout: (a) exact subprocess count per invocation, (b) wall-clock duration per invocation, (c) which of the 9 referenced scripts actually ran versus hit a failed .exists() guard.
The reduced design's regression test asserts the per-turn spawn count is at most 2 (the two scripts confirmed to exist) unless a named exception is documented with a rationale.
issues.acceptance_criteria_source: prd-v2.md section 5, FR-8/FR-8a row; SRS.md:734 (FR-19).

issues.title: PRD FR-21 / SRS FR-33: fix or formally retire the 7 dead Stop-hook script references
issues.build_status: Root-caused; NOT started.
issues.body:
THIS IS A CORRECTNESS DEFECT, SEPARABLE FROM FR-8a's OVERHEAD SCOPE. hooks/stop-notifier.py references 9 scripts. 7 do not exist on disk: archive-old-sessions.py, auto-save-session.py, common-failures-prevention.py, git-auto-commit-policy.py, plan-session-archiver.py, preference-auto-tracker.py, session-pruner.py. Only sync-version.py and voice-notifier.py exist.

Each missing-script .exists() guard fails SILENTLY, every turn, with zero log trace. 7 of 9 advertised behaviours -- auto-save, archiving, common-failure prevention, git auto-commit, plan-session archiving, preference tracking, session pruning -- have NEVER EXECUTED.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN ISSUE: FR-8a as scoped is 'measure and reduce overhead'. It will correctly measure the real 2-spawn floor and could plausibly report 'already optimal' -- TRUE for overhead and FALSE for correctness.

DEPENDENCY THAT IS EASY TO MISS: the retirement path requires the lost capability to appear with a disposition in the FR-12/NFR-10 ledger (V2-006, V2-008). Without that ledger, only the rebuild path remains, and rebuild defers to v2.1. See sequencing_risks.md R-11.

'Silently broken' is not an acceptable end state for either choice.
acceptance_criteria: For each of the 7 missing scripts, exactly one of two states holds and is recorded: (a) the script file exists on disk and its corresponding .exists() guard now evaluates true in a test run, or (b) the reference is removed from hooks/stop_notifier/core.py AND the lost capability appears with a disposition in the FR-12/NFR-10 ledger.
A grep for the 7 filenames inside hooks/stop_notifier/ after remediation returns either a real file or zero references -- never a dangling reference to an absent file.
issues.acceptance_criteria_source: prd-v2.md section 5, FR-21 row; SRS.md:748 (FR-33).

issues.title: PRD NFR-2 / SRS NFR-8: replace fixed pipeline timeouts with 5 non-temporal control mechanisms
issues.build_status: Contradicted on a WIDER surface than Phase 0 scoped. NOT started.
issues.body:
DELETING THE HOOKS DOES NOT SATISFY NFR-2. It satisfies only the hook half of a two-part defect. This is the single most under-scoped item in the original plan: NFR-2 previously shared a 3-point measurement-harness row with NFR-1; split out, it is 8 points, and that is where the real size was hiding.

NFR-2 IS ALREADY VIOLATED INSIDE THE ENGINE, ON THE PIPELINE PATH, INDEPENDENTLY OF HOOKS. 6 timeout= APPLICATION sites across 5 files:
  prompt_gen_expert_caller.py:228
  todo_decomposer.py:147
  orchestrator_agent_caller.py:137
  todo_executor.py:114
  task_orchestration.py:160
  task_orchestration.py:217
Plus 3 DEFINITION sites: STEP1_PROMPT_GEN_TIMEOUT default 60 at prompt_gen_expert_caller.py:54; STEP1_TODO_DECOMPOSER_TIMEOUT default 90 at todo_decomposer.py:37; a function-local read at task_orchestration.py:128.

task_orchestration.py:160 composes to a 75-SECOND FIXED WALL-CLOCK TIMEOUT on the Step 1 pipeline path (_pg_inner_timeout + 15 = 60 + 15). NONE of these 9 sites appears in any Phase 0 artifact -- Phase 0 scoped NFR-2 to the 4 hook timeouts only. The missing 75-second timeout is recorded as one of corrections #9-13.

This is a RESILIENCE-ENGINEERING BUILD, not a scan-and-confirm.

NO DEPENDENCY ON ANY OTHER ISSUE IN THIS PLAN. It sits in batch G only because the D1-D7 gate order is fixed and NFR-2 belongs to D6. If work is parallelised, this is the single best candidate to pull forward: it is the largest sourced item outside the selector, and it blocks nothing and is blocked by nothing.
acceptance_criteria: A static scan for timeout=, signal.alarm, or a subprocess timeout keyword argument returns zero unconditional fixed timeouts on the long-running pipeline path, scanned across BOTH the plugin's bundled code AND the engine pipeline path under langgraph_engine/sdlc_pipeline/architecture/ and langgraph_engine/sdlc_pipeline/nodes/ -- specifically the 6 named application sites and 3 named definition sites.
Any timeout present must be configurable and default to unbounded or user-overridable.
Exactly ONE documented exception is permitted: a single-call socket/HTTP-level I/O timeout that raises a retryable error into a circuit breaker rather than aborting the enclosing pipeline task.

The regression test asserts all 5 ADR-016 mechanisms are present: attempt-count/iteration bound, lease renewal, a convergence (no-progress) signal, a circuit breaker per external dependency with non-fixed reopen-wait, and full-jitter retry.
issues.acceptance_criteria_source: prd-v2.md section 5, NFR-2 row (Phase 2.1 revision per ADR-016); SRS.md:755 (NFR-8).
